title: Long-term podcast clip strategist + editor for top show (data-driven, performance incentives)
description:
I host The Grateful Podcast, a long-form interview show in the top 2.5% globally with 130+ episodes and a growing presence on YouTube, Instagram, LinkedIn, and TikTok. Past guests include David Meltzer, Hala Taha, and Dan Millman.

I'm hiring one person long-term to own short-form clipping across the full library. The model is closer to what Steven Bartlett's team does on Diary of a CEO than a typical clip-and-post freelance gig. This is ongoing work for as long as the show runs.

The work:



New episodes drop weekly. You clip from those.

You also clip from the back catalog. A 6-month-old episode with a strong moment is a clip we haven't made yet. The full 130+ episode library is fair game.

We work from data. Together we review what's performing, identify patterns, and double down on what's working. If a clip from Episode 80 hits, we look at why and reclip in that direction.

Target volume: roughly 40 finished clips per month across platforms.

Turnaround: weekly batch delivery, schedule we agree on together.



Compensation:



Base: starting from $600-$1,000/month depending on experience. Not rock set on this can be discussed further.

***Performance incentives on top of base. 

Clips that hit defined view and engagement thresholds earn bonuses. 

We'll set the thresholds together once we have a baseline.

Paid weekly. Reliable, on-time.



The editing philosophy:

The clip is the story. The editing serves the story. Not the other way around.

What I want:



Crisp cuts. Tight pacing. Dead beats removed.

Clean branded captions, consistent placement, consistent font.

The show logo, subtle, in a fixed position.

Let the moment breathe when the moment deserves it.



What I do not want:



Flashy B-roll cutaways every few seconds.

Exuberant text effects, zoom-bounce, shake, pop animations.

Stock footage layered over the speaker.

Emoji in captions.

Sound effects, swooshes, risers, transitions that announce themselves.

Anything that looks like a TikTok template.



Look at how Diary of a CEO, Lex Fridman, and Modern Wisdom edit their short-form. Simple. Story-led. The face, the words, the captions. That is the bar.

If your portfolio is full of zoom-punch edits and stock B-roll, we're not a fit and that's okay. If your portfolio shows restraint and trust in the speaker, keep reading.

What I'm looking for:



Demonstrated experience clipping podcasts specifically. Not gaming. Not MrBeast-style. Podcasts.

Comfort reading analytics. You can look at a YouTube Studio dashboard or Instagram Insights and tell me what it means.

Strong taste for what makes a story moment land.

Clean caption work. Branded, consistent, readable.

You can articulate why a moment is a clip, not just cut what sounds good.

At least one creator you've worked with for 6 months or longer.



Open to candidates anywhere. Fit and quality first, location second.

To apply, send me:



Three podcast clips you've made for past clients. Links, not attachments.

The name of one creator you've worked with for 6+ months.

Your rate per finished clip and your monthly capacity.

Pick one podcast clip account on Instagram or TikTok whose editing style you respect. In two or three sentences, tell me what they do well and where their restraint shows.



I read every application. I do not respond to generic pitches. If you copy-paste a template, I'll see it and skip you.

Shortlisted candidates will do a paid trial: three clips from one episode, $50-$75 flat. From there, we go long.

Looking forward to seeing your work.

title: Paid Media Specialist — Google & Microsoft Ads
description:
What You Will Do

Campaign Management & Optimization

— Manage Google Ads campaigns across Search, Shopping, Performance Max, and Demand Gen

— Manage Microsoft Ads campaigns with increasing scope as accounts are onboarded

— Build, maintain, and expand negative keyword lists (from ~100 to 500–2,000+ per account)

— Perform weekly search term analysis to identify waste, close variant bleed, and new keyword opportunities

— Suppress zero-conversion products in Shopping feeds and optimize product-level bids

— Execute device, geographic, audience, and ad schedule bid adjustments backed by data

— Consolidate RSA ad copy, remove outdated messaging, and test new creative variations

— Manage cross-brand and cross-campaign overlap to prevent self-competition on shared terms

Conversion Tracking & Measurement

— Monitor and troubleshoot conversion tracking across Google Ads, GA4, Google Tag Manager, and CRM integrations (Salesforce)

— Ensure GCLID, GBRAID, and WBRAID parameters are capturing properly across all web forms

— Validate that conversion actions are active, correctly attributed, and properly categorized (Primary vs. Secondary)

— Track Enhanced Conversions, Customer Match audiences, and offline conversion imports for data quality

— Implement and maintain call tracking (Dynamic Number Insertion) and form submission tracking

Analysis & Reporting

— Produce regular performance reports covering spend, ROAS, conversion volume, cost-per-conversion, and impression share

— Analyze campaign, ad group, keyword, product, landing page, device, and geographic performance to surface actionable insights

— Document analysis and recommendations in writing before presenting to the founder for approval

— Monitor competitive metrics (impression share, overlap rate, outranking share) and flag shifts

— Identify landing page quality gaps and coordinate with the team on page-level improvements

Account Growth & Expansion

— Support Performance Max campaign reactivation and testing with proper asset groups and conversion signals

— Build and manage remarketing and audience strategies across Google and Microsoft

— Identify impression share expansion opportunities and model incremental revenue impact

— Assist with onboarding new client accounts into the paid media workflow as the agency grows



What This Role Is Not

— Not an SEO, social media, or content marketing role

— Not a general virtual assistant or admin role

— Not client-facing account management (founder handles client communication)

— Not a graphic design or landing page development role

— Not an autonomous role on day one — you earn expanded ownership through demonstrated performance



How We Work: The Approval Model

This is important to understand before you apply. We manage significant client ad spend, and every dollar matters. Our workflow operates on an analysis-first, approval-before-execution model:



— Identify — You find the issue or opportunity in the data (waste, underperformance, untapped keyword, bid gap, etc.)

— Analyze — You quantify the impact, pull the supporting data, and document your reasoning

— Recommend — You present the recommendation to the founder with the evidence that supports it

— Execute — After approval, you implement the change and track the result



Routine maintenance tasks (search term negatives, bid adjustments within established guardrails, ad copy fixes) will have pre-approved parameters you can act on independently. Structural changes — campaign restructures, budget shifts, new campaign launches, conversion action changes — always require approval. This workflow is designed to protect the client and build mutual trust. Candidates who find this restrictive are not the right fit. Candidates who recognize this as a structured path to full ownership are.



Tools You Will Use

You must be proficient in the core paid media toolset. Training provided for agency-specific workflows and internal tools.



— Google Ads — Search, Shopping, Performance Max, Demand Gen (required)

— Microsoft Ads (required)

— Google Analytics 4 / GA4 (required)

— Google Tag Manager (required)

— Google Merchant Center (required)

— Google Sheets / Docs / Drive (required)

— Google Ads Editor + Microsoft Ads Editor (strongly preferred)

— Salesforce or equivalent CRM (familiarity preferred — for conversion pipeline understanding)

— Slack (daily communication)

— Asana (task management tool familiarity — Asana preferred)



Must-Haves

— Minimum 2 years managing Google Ads accounts with significant monthly spend ($10K+/month, higher preferred)

— Hands-on experience with Search, Shopping, and Performance Max campaign types

— Strong understanding of conversion tracking: Google Tag, GA4 events, GCLID attribution, Enhanced Conversions, and offline conversion imports

— Experience building and maintaining negative keyword strategies at scale

— Ability to analyze campaign data at the keyword, product, ad group, device, geographic, and landing page level and draw actionable conclusions

— Experience with Google Ads Editor for bulk changes

— Working knowledge of Google Merchant Center and product feed optimization

— Microsoft Ads experience (campaign management, import from Google, UET tracking)

— Strong analytical skills — you think in ROAS, CPA, and margin, not just clicks and CTR

— Ability to write clear analysis summaries and document recommendations before execution

— Strong written English — you will present findings and recommendations in writing regularly

— Available Monday–Friday with at least 3–4 hours of overlap with US Eastern 9 AM–1 PM

— Detail-oriented and process-driven — mistakes on a $1M account are expensive

— Reliable internet connection with a backup plan



Nice-to-Haves (Not Required, But You Will Stand Out)

— Experience managing $50K+/month in ad spend across Google and Microsoft

— Experience with B2B lead generation campaigns (not just e-commerce)

— Familiarity with Salesforce conversion pipelines and offline conversion tracking

— Experience with Dynamic Number Insertion (DNI) for call tracking

— Google Ads certification (Search, Shopping, or Measurement)

— Experience managing multi-brand or multi-storefront accounts with cross-campaign coordination

— Familiarity with landing page testing and CRO principles

— Background in agency environments managing paid media across multiple client accounts

— Experience with auction insights analysis and competitive share-of-voice reporting



Hours & Working Style

— Starts part-time: 15–25 hours per week, with a clear path to full-time as you take on day-to-day management and additional client accounts

— Long-term engagement — we are building a paid media function inside a growing agency

— Consistent daily availability required — ad accounts need monitoring, not sporadic large blocks

— At least 3–4 hours daily overlap with US Eastern 9 AM–1 PM for real-time collaboration and approvals

— Clear, proactive communication is non-negotiable — if something looks wrong in the data, flag it immediately

— You will work alongside the founder (strategy, client relationships, approvals) and coordinate with our SEO and execution teams on cross-channel priorities



What We Offer

We treat contractors like tea
mbers. After a 90-day evaluation period, you become eligible for the following perks:



— Prorated 13th Month Payment — Paid in December or at year-end close, prorated based on months actively engaged after eligibility.

— Paid Time Off — 40 hours (5 days) of PTO upon successful completion of the 90-day evaluation period. After one full year of engagement, this increases to 80 hours (10 days) annually.

— Sick / Emergency Time — Reasonable notice required. Specific terms defined during onboarding.

— Remote Work Allowance — $25 to $50 USD/month to support your internet, power, and workspace costs. Exact amount confirmed in writing based on performance and continued engagement.

— Recognized Holidays — Blended Philippine and US holiday calendar agreed upon during onboarding.

— Performance Bonus — Discretionary and based on quality, reliability, output, client impact, and role-specific KPIs.

— Full-Time Conversion — Strong performers during the evaluation period will be offered a transition to full-time hours with expanded scope and additional client accounts.



90-Day Evaluation Period: The first 90 days are a mutual evaluation period. During this time, we assess reliability, analytical quality, turnaround time, communication, attention to detail, and ability to work within our approval workflow. Contractor perks and full-time consideration begin after successful completion of this period.



How to Apply

Please start your proposal with the word ROAS so we know you read the full post.



In your proposal, please answer the following:



1. You open a Google Ads account and see that Performance Max campaigns are spending 40% of budget at a 1.85x blended ROAS, but the top 5 campaigns averaged 2.77x while the bottom 4 averaged 0.55x. All PMax campaigns were paused by a previous manager. What is your approach?

2. An e-commerce account has only 117 negative keywords and you find $131K in spend on 3,100+ search terms with zero conversions. Walk us through how you would prioritize and build the negative keyword list.

3. Are you comfortable in a role where you present analysis and recommendations to the founder for approval before making changes, especially in the first 90–180 days?



If you have case studies, audit samples, or screenshots showing Google Ads performance improvements you contributed to, please include them. We are especially interested in seeing how you think through account problems, not just before-and-after numbers.

title: WordPress Developer — Elementor
description:
Summary

We are a US-based digital marketing agency that builds and manages WordPress websites for professional services clients across legal, e-commerce, healthcare, travel, landscaping, retail, and nonprofit. We currently manage seven active client sites and are growing. Every site runs on WordPress with Elementor as the primary page builder.



We need a WordPress Developer who can build and ship client-facing websites and pages at agency pace. Our current bottleneck is web development speed — projects that should take weeks are taking months. If you can take a wireframe, a brand direction, and a set of page requirements and turn them into a polished, mobile-responsive, fast-loading WordPress site using Elementor without constant hand-holding, this role is for you.



This role starts part-time (15–30 hours/week) and has a clear path to full-time as the client portfolio grows. There is no shortage of work — we need someone who can keep up with it.



A portfolio is required. Proposals without links to live WordPress sites you have built will not be considered.



What Agency Pace Means

We want to be direct about this because it is the reason this role exists. In an agency environment, web development moves on client timelines, not open-ended project timelines. Here is what we consider normal throughput for this role:



— A full client website (5–10 pages, standard service business) should move from approved wireframe to staging review in 2–3 weeks, not 2–3 months

— A single landing page or interior page build should take hours, not days

— Page revisions based on feedback should be turned around within 24–48 hours

— You should be able to manage 2–3 active projects simultaneously without losing quality or missing deadlines



If you are someone who needs weeks to build a single page or frequently misses deadlines, this is not the right fit. If you are fast, organized, and take pride in shipping clean work on schedule, you will do very well here.



What You Will Do

Website Builds & Page Development

— Build complete client websites in WordPress using Elementor Theme Builder from wireframes, mockups, or detailed page briefs provided by the founder

— Create and customize page templates, headers, footers, archive pages, single post templates, and dynamic content layouts in Elementor

— Build service pages, landing pages, blog layouts, contact pages, about pages, team pages, and other standard business site pages

— Implement mobile-responsive design across all breakpoints — every page must look clean on desktop, tablet, and mobile

— Build on staging environments and push to production after founder review and approval

WordPress Administration & Plugin Management

— Install, configure, and troubleshoot WordPress plugins including forms (Gravity Forms, WPForms, Contact Form 7), SEO (Rank Math), caching, security, and image optimization (Imagify)

— Manage WordPress updates (core, theme, plugins) and resolve conflicts or issues that arise from updates

— Configure domain connections, SSL, hosting environment settings, and DNS as needed

— Set up and maintain staging environments for safe development and testing

— Troubleshoot site issues — broken layouts, plugin conflicts, slow load times, form errors, 404s — and resolve them without being asked twice

Performance & Quality

— Optimize page speed and Core Web Vitals — compress images, minimize CSS/JS, configure caching, and lazy-load media

— Ensure cross-browser compatibility (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge)

— Implement basic on-page SEO structure as directed (heading hierarchy, alt text, meta fields via Rank Math)

— Follow brand guidelines for each client — correct fonts, colors, spacing, and imagery across all pages

— QA every page before submitting for review — check links, forms, responsive breakpoints, and load times

Collaboration & Process

— Work from clear briefs and wireframes provided by the founder — ask clarifying questions early, not after building the wrong thing

— Provide time estimates for each build and communicate proactively if timelines shift

— Document reusable templates, section libraries, and build patterns so the team can scale

— Coordinate with the content and SEO teams when builds require content integration or technical SEO implementation



What This Role Is Not

— Not a design role — you will receive wireframes, mockups, and brand direction; you are not creating concepts from scratch

— Not an SEO strategist, content writer, or marketing role

— Not a custom PHP developer or theme coder — we build with Elementor, not custom code (though basic CSS/HTML for adjustments is expected)

— Not a general virtual assistant or admin role

— Not client-facing — the founder handles all client communication



Tools You Will Use

You must be highly proficient in WordPress and Elementor. Training provided for agency-specific workflows only.



— WordPress (required — this is the entire job)

— Elementor Pro / Elementor Theme Builder (required — non-negotiable)

— Rank Math (required — for on-page SEO field entry)

— Gravity Forms, WPForms, or Contact Form 7 (required)

— Imagify or ShortPixel (image optimization)

— WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, or equivalent caching plugin

— Google PageSpeed Insights / GTmetrix (performance testing)

— Canva (basic asset resizing and formatting — not design work)

— Google Drive / Docs / Sheets (file and brief management)

— Slack (daily communication)

— Asana (task management tool familiarity — Asana Preferred)

— Staging environments (Bluehost, WP Engine, or equivalent — familiarity required)



Must-Haves

— Portfolio required — you must include links to live WordPress sites you have built or significantly contributed to. Proposals without a portfolio will not be reviewed.

— Minimum 2 years building WordPress websites using Elementor (not just minor edits — full site builds)

— Strong proficiency with Elementor Theme Builder including custom headers, footers, archive templates, and dynamic content

— Demonstrated ability to build a complete business website (5–10 pages) from wireframe to staging in 2–3 weeks

— Experience managing multiple WordPress plugins and resolving plugin conflicts

— Mobile-responsive design skills — your sites must look polished on every device

— Page speed optimization experience — you know how to get pages loading fast without sacrificing quality

— Comfortable working in staging environments and following a staging-to-production deployment workflow

— Basic CSS and HTML for fine-tuning layouts, spacing, and responsive adjustments beyond what Elementor handles natively

— Experience working across multiple client websites simultaneously without mixing up branding, assets, or instructions

— Strong written English — clear communication on timelines, blockers, and questions is essential

— Available Monday–Friday with at least 3 hours of overlap with US Eastern 9 AM–12 PM

— Reliable internet connection with a backup plan



Nice-to-Haves (Not Required, But You Will Stand Out)

— Experience building sites for professional services clients (law firms, healthcare, B2B companies)

— Familiarity with WooCommerce setup and product page builds

— Experience with Elementor custom code widgets or Elementor Pro integrations

— Background in an agency environment building sites for multiple clients on rotation

— Experience with Google Tag Manager container installation and basic conversion tracking setup

— Familiarity with accessibility basics (WCAG compliance, ADA considerations)

— Experience with domain migration, site cloning, or hosting transfers

— Familiarity with Bluehost or WP Engine hosting environments



Hours & Working Style

— Starts part-time: 15–30 hours per week, with a clear path to full-time as the client portfolio grows and build volume increases

— Long-term engagement — we have a growing pipeline of client sites that need building and ongoing maintenance

— Consistent daily availability preferred — web builds move in sprints and require steady progress, not sporadic blocks

— At least 3 hours daily overlap with US Eastern 9 AM–12 PM for feedback loops and approvals

— You will receive detailed briefs and wireframes — your job is to build fast, build clean, and flag blockers early

— You will work alongside the founder (creative direction, client communication, approvals) and coordinate with our content and SEO teams on site launches



What We Offer

We treat contractors like tea
mbers. After a 90-day evaluation period, you become eligible for the following perks:



— Prorated 13th Month Payment — Paid in December or at year-end close, prorated based on months actively engaged after eligibility.

— Paid Time Off — 40 hours (5 days) of PTO upon successful completion of the 90-day evaluation period. After one full year of engagement, this increases to 80 hours (10 days) annually.

— Sick / Emergency Time — Reasonable notice required. Specific terms defined during onboarding.

— Remote Work Allowance — $25 to $50 USD/month to support your internet, power, and workspace costs. Exact amount confirmed in writing based on performance and continued engagement.

— Recognized Holidays — Blended Philippine and US holiday calendar agreed upon during onboarding.

— Performance Bonus — Discretionary and based on quality, reliability, build speed, and client impact.

— Full-Time Conversion — Strong performers during the evaluation period will be offered a transition to full-time hours with expanded responsibilities.



90-Day Evaluation Period: The first 90 days are a mutual evaluation period. During this time, we assess build quality, speed, communication, attention to detail, mobile responsiveness, and ability to manage multiple projects. Contractor perks and full-time consideration begin after successful completion of this period.



How to Apply

Please start your proposal with the word BUILD so we know you read the full post.



In your proposal, please include the following:



1. Links to 2–3 live WordPress sites you built using Elementor. For each, briefly describe your role (full build vs. specific pages), the timeline from start to launch, and any plugins you integrated. This is mandatory — proposals without portfolio links will not be reviewed.

2. A client needs a 7-page professional services website (Home, About, 3 Service pages, Blog, Contact) with a custom header/footer, mobile responsiveness, contact form integration, and basic SEO fields populated. You receive the wireframe and brand assets on day one. How long does it take you to deliver a staging-ready build, and what does your process look like?

3. Are you comfortable working on multiple client sites simultaneously where strategy and creative direction come from the founder, and your focus is building fast and building clean?

Are you great at communicating with others? Are you meticulous and organized? Do you love automating tasks? Let’s team up.



We believe in people. This is why we only work with clients who serve people. From firefighters, to law firms, to suppliers sending life-saving food to kids dying of malnutrition, the work you do will help make the world a better place.



Our team is made up of people who want to do the best work of their life. People who love to learn, challenge themselves, grow and have some fun along the journey. We also care about each other – we support each other in our own personal goals and vision. We are human beings before employees and we love to bring out the best in each other.



Now, ready to learn more about this opening? Buckle up.



If you work here, you’ll be:

- Challenged to do the best work of your life in a supportive environment.

- Become the best communicator you can become (this is the most important thing we do).

- Have the space to ask questions, voice your feedback and make a difference (and be yourself).

- Help drive our projects and tools, participate in stimulating conversations, and grow with like-minded people.



What you could be working on:

- Oversight of our fast growth projects and understanding the nuances

- Communicate status, progress, ensuring "nothing slips through the cracks"

- Build and voice your opinion on key project features

- Communicate and help developers understand various tasks

- Testing new features to ensure it meets project needs

- Research, engaging customers via
/chat, proof reading, copywriting, organizing events, etc 



You’ll do well in this job if you:

- Are a master at the English language and care about writing well

- Enjoy using and learning about technology and being helpful

- Enjoy working with people who actually care about what they do and will not let you be lazy or do sloppy work.

- Have an opinion and care about best practices and love learning and creating and building.

- Have grit and determination and are someone who will exceed no matter what gets in your way.

- Are attentive to details.

- Have experience in n8n to help with various team and project automations (required)



You probably shouldn’t apply if:

- You’re “just looking for extra money.”

- You like working 5 full-time jobs because all you care about is work.

- You get offended easily and take things personally.

- You are not someone with grit and determination who can persevere while being challenged to do great work.

- You get overwhelmed easily, new habits, new learnings and chat messages.



The interview process:

- Since 99% of our work is done via Slack (we don’t do scheduled calls), the entire interview process will be via
. (With lots of questions, sprinkled with a few voice notes)



If you work here:

- You’ll get 13th month salary, Filipino holidays, unlimited time off (we don’t count sick days), a normal working day schedule (no night shifts, although an early start is preferred for time overlap) with some flexibility, a week off during the holidays in December, and the opportunity to grow and become your best self.



A little more about us:

- We’ve been in business for a decade+. Our teams are remote (mostly in the Philippines, about 20 people). Our longest standing tea
mber has been with us for over 14+ years. We've had people quit smoking on our teams with our help, lose weight, learn a new instrument, speak a new language, and more. We all love what we do.



How to begin

- Your mission, should you choose to accept, is to send us an
 with 3 questions you have about this role. If you’re currently in a full-time role and are looking for something new, we’re open to a transition window. We actually care about your happiness.



NOTE: While we like AI, and we use it in certain circumstances, we ask that no AI be used during communication. Communication is the most important thing we do. If I don't see your natural voice from our first interaction, then you're setting an inaccurate representation of who you are and how you communicate. And when I see that change, it's going to come across as a lack of harmony in how you communicate.

title: Phone Appointment Setter - US Battery Backup Program (Not Solar)
description:
About the role



  You're the first voice on the phone for the Texas Grid Resilience Project - a battery-backup and lower-rate energy program for Texas homeowners. You don't sell. You don't quote prices. You don't visit anyone's house. Your one job is to confirm that the person on the phone owns their home, make crystal clear that this is NOT solar (no roof panels, no solar loan, we do not touch the roof), and book them onto a US-based specialist's calendar for a 10-minute follow-up call.



This is appointment setting, not closing. The specialist does the heavy lifting. You get them to the appointment.



What you'll do every shift



  - Work through a queue of pre-loaded Texas homeowner leads in our dialer

  - Follow the script

  - Qualify: homeowner (not renter), on the utility bill, can text a breaker-panel photo, understands this is a phone call and not a home visit

  - Pivot to the appointment by offering two specific time windows, never as a yes/no question

  - Use the rebuttal library inside the live dialer — no improvising on objections

  - Disposition every call cleanly and log notes the QA team can read

  - Roll into weekly QA review knowing every call is recorded and a sample is scored



Compensation



  - Hourly base, paid weekly

  - Appointment commission (held until the appointment is confirmed)

  - Weekly leaderboard with a cash prize for the top performer; bottom of the week is flagged for review



  A strong setter's bonuses meaningfully outpace base. We will give you exact numbers in the interview.



Schedule



  - US Central business hours, mostly afternoons and early evenings

  - Monday through Saturday — we do not call on Sundays

  - Minimum hours/week confirmed at offer



Equipment and workspace



  - Reliable wired internet (no public WiFi, no shared mobile hotspots during shifts)

  - A computer that runs Chrome smoothly

  - Noise-canceling headset with a quality mic

  - A quiet, professional-sounding workspace — no background TV, no kids in the room, no dogs barking. All calls are recorded; ambient

  noise gets flagged.



Who we're hiring



  - Comfortable making outbound calls to US homeowners

  - Clear, friendly English at a pace customers don't have to ask you to repeat

  - Coachable — you'll get QA feedback weekly and you'll act on it

  - Disciplined about the script: the opener, the not-solar disclaimer, and the ownership question are non-negotiable

  - Bonus: experience in energy, home services, insurance, or any phone-based appointment setting



Hard lines — single-strike compliance



  - Saying or implying this is solar

  - Claiming to be from the utility company

  - Guaranteeing savings of any amount

  - Telling the customer they are "approved" before specialist verification

  - Ignoring a do-not-call request



   Cross any of these once and your access is revoked while we review the recording. We don't bend on these.



How hiring works (wave-based)



  1. Short prescreen (US Central availability, outbound experience, equipment check, ownership-question comfort)

  2. Application + voice recording sample

  3. Written test on the rebuttals and the not-solar disclaimer

  4. Compliance agreement

  5. Mock-call evaluation

  6. Paid one-week live trial with QA scoring

  7. Decision: hired, extended, or released



  If "not solar, not solar, not solar" is already echoing in your head, you're ahead of most applicants. Apply.

title: Technical SEO & GEO Specialist
description:
Summary

We are a US-based digital marketing and revenue operations agency that manages SEO, content, and web optimization across a portfolio of seven active clients spanning e-commerce, legal, travel, healthcare, retail, landscaping, and nonprofit.



We are hiring a Technical SEO & GEO Specialist to own organic search performance across this portfolio. You will not be publishing blog posts or scheduling social media. You will be the person who diagnoses why a site is underperforming, builds the optimization roadmap, and directs our execution team on exactly what to fix. You will work directly with the founder — not a middle manager — on strategy, audits, and client priorities.



This role starts part-time (10–20 hours/week) and has a clear path to full-time if performance is strong during the initial evaluation period. We are building a team, not filling a temporary gap.



This role exists because search is changing. AI-driven search experiences are reshaping how businesses get found, and we need someone who understands both traditional technical SEO and generative engine optimization well enough to keep our clients visible as that shift accelerates. If you are tired of execution-only roles and want to own SEO outcomes across a real, revenue-generating client portfolio, this is built for you.



What You Will Own

Technical SEO Strategy & Audits

— Perform comprehensive technical SEO audits for existing and net-new clients using our audit framework, and contribute improvements to the framework over time

— Diagnose crawl, indexation, rendering, and structured data issues using Google Search Console, Screaming Frog, Ahrefs, or equivalent tools

— Develop and prioritize optimization roadmaps based on audit findings, search data, and business impact

— Review and improve site architecture, internal linking strategies, URL structures, and crawl efficiency

— Audit and implement schema markup (FAQ, LocalBusiness, Article, HowTo, etc.) across client sites

On-Page & Content Optimization Direction

— Define on-page optimization requirements for blog posts, service pages, and location pages (meta titles, descriptions, heading structure, keyword targeting, internal links)

— Create clear, actionable optimization briefs that the execution team can implement without ambiguity

— Review published content for SEO quality and flag issues before they compound

— Guide keyword targeting and content gap analysis to inform the editorial calendar

GEO / Generative Engine Optimization

— Optimize client content for visibility in AI-generated search results, featured snippets, and answer engine experiences

— Structure content to satisfy entity-based search, question-intent queries, and knowledge graph signals

— Stay current on how Google SGE, Bing Copilot, Perplexity, and ChatGPT Search surface and cite content, and adapt strategies accordingly

— Implement and refine structured data to improve content eligibility for rich results and AI citations

Reporting & Founder Collaboration

— Track key SEO metrics (rankings, organic traffic, indexation, CTR, featured snippet capture) and report on progress

— Join weekly or biweekly syncs with the founder to discuss strategy, audit findings, and client priorities

— Document recurring SEO processes and build lightweight SOPs as workflows stabilize



What This Role Is Not

— Not a blog-writing or content-creation role (we have writers and an execution team for that)

— Not a general virtual assistant or admin role

— Not client-facing account management

— Not social media management or graphic design

— Not WordPress development or plugin/theme coding



Tools You Will Use

Training provided for any tools you have not used before, but you must be proficient in the core SEO toolset.



— Google Search Console (required)

— Ahrefs or SEMrush (required — Ahrefs preferred)

— WordPress with Rank Math (required)

— Google Analytics / GA4 (required)

— Screaming Frog or similar crawler (strongly preferred)

— Google Sheets / Docs / Drive (required)

— Schema markup generators or manual JSON-LD (required)

— Slack (daily communication)

— Asana (task management tool familiarity — Asana preferred)



Must-Haves

— Minimum 2 years of hands-on technical SEO experience (not just content SEO or on-page basics)

— Demonstrated ability to run a technical SEO audit end-to-end and produce actionable findings

— Strong understanding of site architecture, crawl budget, indexation, Core Web Vitals, and structured data

— Working knowledge of GEO / generative engine optimization concepts and how AI search is evolving

— Experience with schema markup implementation (JSON-LD preferred)

— Proficiency with Ahrefs or SEMrush for keyword research, backlink analysis, and site audits

— Strong WordPress experience, including Rank Math configuration

— Ability to write clear optimization briefs and technical recommendations that a non-technical executor can follow

— Strong written English — communication is critical in this role

— Available Monday–Friday with at least 3 hours of overlap with US Eastern 9 AM–12 PM

— Detail-oriented — we serve professional services clients (lawyers, healthcare) where errors are a serious problem

— Reliable internet connection with a backup plan



Nice-to-Haves (Not Required, But You Will Stand Out)

— Experience with local SEO (Google Business Profile optimization, citation building, local pack strategy)

— Familiarity with log file analysis for crawl diagnostics

— Experience managing or directing junior SEO executors

— Background in agency environments or managing SEO across multiple client accounts simultaneously

— Understanding of programmatic SEO or template-based page optimization

— Experience with Ahrefs Brand Radar or AI visibility monitoring tools

— Familiarity with NLP-driven content optimization tools (Surfer, Clearscope, Frase, or similar)



Hours & Working Style

— Starts part-time: 10–20 hours per week, with a clear path to full-time based on performance during the evaluation period

— Long-term engagement — we are building a team, not filling a one-off project

— Consistent weekly availability preferred over sporadic large blocks

— At least 3 hours daily overlap with US Eastern 9 AM–12 PM for real-time collaboration

— Clear, proactive communication matters more than total hours logged

— You will work alongside our execution VA (WordPress, publishing, formatting) and the founder (strategy, client relationships)



What We Offer

We treat contractors like tea
mbers. After a 90-day evaluation period, you become eligible for the following perks with graduation into full-time status:



— Prorated 13th Month Payment — Paid in December or at year-end close, prorated based on months actively engaged after eligibility.

— Paid Time Off — 40 hours (5 days) of PTO upon successful completion of the 90-day evaluation period. After one full year of engagement, this increases to 80 hours (10 days) annually.

— Sick / Emergency Time — Reasonable notice required. Specific terms defined during onboarding.

— Remote Work Allowance — $25 to $50 USD/month to support your internet, power, and workspace costs. Exact amount confirmed in writing based on performance and continued engagement.

— Recognized Holidays — Blended Philippine and US holiday calendar agreed upon during onboarding.

— Performance Bonus — Discretionary and based on quality, reliability, output, client impact, and role-specific KPIs.

— Full-Time Conversion — Strong performers during the evaluation period will be offered a transition to full-time hours with expanded scope and responsibilities.



90-Day Evaluation Period: The first 90 days are a mutual evaluation period. During this time, we assess reliability, work quality, turnaround time, communication, attention to detail, and tool adoption. Contractor perks and full-time consideration begin after successful completion of this period.



How to Apply

Please start your proposal with the word OPTIMIZE so we know you read the full post.



In your proposal, please answer the following:



1. Describe a technical SEO issue you identified during an audit and how you resolved it.

2. What is one thing most SEOs get wrong about optimizing for AI-driven search (GEO/AEO) in 2026?

3. Are you comfortable in a role where you own strategy recommendations but the founder makes final decisions on direction?



If you have a portfolio, audit sample, or case study showing SEO results you contributed to, please include it.

title: Xero Forensics & Cleanup Expert - Fix Messy Books
description:
This is a hands-on Xero rescue role: you’ll walk into messy, behind-the-scenes accounting, diagnose what’s broken, and deliver clean, report-ready books quickly — with minimal hand-holding. This is for a calm expert who owns outcomes, not an entry-level data-entry role.



What this role will actually involve

- Triage messy Xero files and produce a prioritized remediation plan within the first week.

- Bring bank/credit card/loan accounts up to date — reconcile overdue periods and clear unexplained variances.

- Categorize and reclassify large volumes of uncoded or mis-coded transactions so P&L & balance sheet make sense.

- Locate and remove duplicates; recreate or correct missing entries with supporting documentation.

- Rationalize and clean the Chart of Accounts so reporting is meaningful and month-ends are reliable.

- Fix payroll liability, GST/VAT, and supplier/AP mismatches until accounts tie out.

- Stabilize files from incomplete handovers and document all assumptions, adjustments, and unresolved items.

- Produce concise remediation notes: what you found, exactly what you fixed, remaining risks, and what you need to finish.

- Implement practical controls or process changes to prevent reoccurrence (lightweight, actionable).

- Prepare books and supporting notes so an accountant can pick up clean, auditable months.



What I need from the right person

- Deep, practical Xero expertise (bank rules, repeating journals, reconciliation tools, tracking categories, manual journals).

- Proven track record of catch-up and cleanup work on messy historical books.

- Fast diagnostic ability: quickly form a prioritized plan and execute with minimal oversight.

- Ownership mentality: you deliver the outcome and clearly communicate status and blockers.

- Commercial judgement — you know which fixes matter for reporting and cash decisions.

- Clear, blunt, useful communication: say what’s broken, what you fixed, and what still needs attention.

- Comfortable making documented judgement calls when records are incomplete.

- Organized, rapid, and not fazed by chaos.



Examples of messy situations you’ll fix

- Bank unreconciled for 6+ months with missing bank statements.

- Hundreds of uncoded transactions after a payments-processor migration.

- Duplicated supplier payments and missing invoices.

- Bloated Chart of Accounts with legacy/duplicate codes.

- Payroll liabilities not matching reported balances.



Success in this role (30/60/90)

- 30 days: Triage complete, priority plan in place, high-risk reconciliations started.

- 60 days: Major accounts reconciled, COA rationalized, most catch-up months closed.

- 90 days: Recent months report-ready, cleanup documented, repeatable month-end routine established, and simple controls implemented.



Final note

Tell the truth quickly — I prefer blunt clarity over vague status updates. If you can own messy Xero files and deliver clean, usable books, apply.

title: Outbound Appointment Setter — Cold Calling & Lead Generation Specialist
description:
We’re hiring a confident, outcome-focused Virtual Assistant to run cold-calling outreach using our knowledge base. This is not a script-reader role — you’ll use structured content and product knowledge to engage prospects, qualify leads, and book qualified meetings. Quick thinking, clear communication, and disciplined note-taking into our knowledge base are essential.





What you’ll do

- Use our knowledge base and call scripts as a starting point — adapt language to each prospect naturally.

- Make outbound cold calls to prospects on supplied lists (phone + CRM).

- Qualify leads to a tight brief: needs, budget range, timeline, decision-makers, and next steps.

- Book discovery/demo calls directly on the calendar for our sales team.

- Log call outcomes, notes, and follow-up tasks in the knowledge base and CRM immediately after each call.

- Run follow-up calls and reminder sequences per playbook until prospect responds or is disqualified.

- Escalate complex or technical questions to the assigned SME and update the knowledge base with new FAQs or clarifications.

- Hit daily/weekly call and meeting targets and maintain call quality standards.

- Provide short weekly reports: calls made, contacts reached, qualified leads, common objections, and suggested knowledge-base updates.



Who we’re looking for

- Comfortable with cold calling and objection handling — you don’t hang up early.

- Strong verbal communication and fast thinker on the phone.

- Able to learn and reference a product/service knowledge base quickly and accurately.

- CRM-savvy (HubSpot, Pipedrive, Salesforce, or similar) and disciplined about logging data.

- Reliable, punctual, and professional on calls.

- Persistent but respectful — you push for outcomes without being spammy.

- Able to follow a playbook but adapt language to sound human and relevant.

- Comfortable with performance tracking and meeting weekly targets.



Tools & systems

- You’ll work from our shared knowledge base (structured articles, objection scripts, product sheets).

- CRM access for logging and call lists.

- Calendar tool for booking meetings.

- Must have a quiet workspace and reliable internet/phone setup.



Performance expectations

- Daily: X outbound calls (we’ll agree target), accurate CRM updates for each call.

- Weekly: Y qualified meetings booked (target set during onboarding).

- Quality: Clear call notes, correct qualification per our brief, and timely knowledge-base updates where needed.



What success looks like in 30/60/90 days

- 30 days: Confidently navigating the knowledge base, meeting call activity targets, regularly qualifying leads to brief.

- 60 days: Consistently hitting meeting-booking goals, reducing average time to qualify, contributing useful knowledge-base improvements.

- 90 days: Reliable pipeline contributor, few errors in CRM logging, proactive in proposing refinements to scripts and playbooks.



Apply only if you have real cold-calling experience and can demonstrate consistent results. In your application, answer briefly:

1. How many outbound cold calls did you make per day in your last role, and what meeting/qualified-lead rate did you achieve?

2. Describe how you would use a knowledge base during a call when a prospect asks a technical question you don’t know the answer to.

Apply with the four items above. I'll respond within 48 hours.

You take our hero assets (artwork imagery, raw clips, big concepts) and produce the social output. You design in Figma. You cut Reels. You post. You engage. You own the social channels day to day. This is a production role, not a strategy role. We have the brand system locked down. You pick it up and produce from it.



THE SHAPE OF YOUR DAY



Your shift is roughly 7am to 3pm Manila time, overlapping Australian business hours so we work together live.

- Mornings cover live US customer engagement, our peak selling window. DMs, comments, follow-ups.

- Afternoons are for content production. Cutting Reels, designing in Figma, scheduling, prepping assets.



WHAT YOU'LL DO



Design and production (60%)

- Design Instagram,
 and 
 carousels, posts and story sequences in Figma

- Cut Reels and short-form video from supplied raw clips (CapCut or Adobe Premiere Pro)

- Adapt our hero artwork imagery into platform-native content

- Maintain visual consistency with our brand system (we provide the design tokens and templates)

- Repurpose long-form content into clips, stories and carousels



Posting and scheduling (15%)

- Daily scheduled posting across Instagram,
 and 

- Story uploads and management

- Hashtag and caption research

- Best-time-to-post optimisation per platform



Engagement (25%)

- Respond to Instagram and
 
 (warm, friendly, helpful)

- Reply to comments on organic and paid posts

- Engage with relevant accounts to build community

- Follow up warm leads from DMs



Ways of working

- Track your hours in Clockify against tasks (no screenshots or monitoring software, just honest time logging)

- Manage tasks and check in daily via ClickUp, with a weekly video call



WHAT WE NEED



Core skills (non-negotiable)

- 3+ years running brand Instagram and
 accounts (show us your work)

- Expert-level Reel and short-form video editing in CapCut or Adobe Premiere Pro (pacing, transitions and beat sync matter more than filters)

- Native-fluent in Figma. This is how we work together, you design in a shared file and we iterate live

- Adobe Creative Suite proficiency (Photoshop at minimum, Premiere Pro a strong plus)

- Clear written English for warm, friendly DM engagement



Tools you'll use

- Figma (primary design, shared workspace)

- Adobe Photoshop and Premiere Pro

- CapCut

- Claude or ChatGPT (we train you on Claude as our main AI hub)

- A social scheduling tool (Later, Metricool, Buffer or your preference)

- Clockify (time tracking) and ClickUp (task management)



Nice-to-haves

- TikTok native experience

- Canva Pro fluency

- A background in BPO or customer-facing roles



Must-haves

- A computer that runs Adobe Premiere Pro and Figma smoothly (16GB RAM minimum, SSD preferred)

- Reliable internet with a backup plan for outages

- A working webcam and a quiet environment

- A portfolio that shows brand consistency, not just individual posts. Show us an account's arc over time

- At least one Reel you produced with 5,000+ views

- Available to work hours that overlap Australian Eastern business hours (roughly 7am to 3pm Manila time)

- Willing to learn new tools and take direction on our process



WHAT YOU GET

- $600 to $900 USD per month, based on experience and portfolio

- 13th month bonus paid every December

- Paid leave after 6 months

- Full-time, 40 hours per week

- Paid trial: a 2-week checkpoint, then a 1-month review, then a long-term agreement once both sides are happy

- A long-term role with a brand that's just launching. You'll be one of our first hires and grow with us



HOW TO APPLY

Start your reply with the word ORIGINAL in all caps. If you don't, your application will be skipped. We read every application, but only from people who follow instructions.



Then include:
